title: Dragon Acid-Base Titration Pool
description: A crystalline dragon hovers above a chemistry pool filled with a reactive liquid solution. The user must perform a multi-step acid-base titration by commanding the dragon to disperse precise amounts of acid or base reagent into the pool, monitoring pH changes through color shifts, and reaching a target neutralization endpoint within tolerance.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements an interactive acid-base titration simulation. Load both GLB assets using GLTFLoader from a CDN. Place the pool model at the scene origin representing a large titration vessel filled with a colored liquid plane (a semi-transparent MeshPhysicalMaterial plane inside the pool). Position the DragonDispersion model hovering above the pool, gently bobbing with a sine-wave animation. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 5, 10) looking at the pool center, with OrbitControls for rotation. Add ambient light intensity 0.6, a directional light from above-right, and a point light near the dragon with a subtle glow. The simulation tracks a pH value starting at 2.0 (strongly acidic, pool liquid colored red). Display a pH meter HUD overlay showing current pH, target pH (7.0 ± 0.3), and a color-coded pH strip. Interaction steps: (1) Click a UI button to select reagent type: strong base NaOH or weak base NH3. (2) Use a slider to set dispensing volume from 1-50 mL per drop. (3) Click the dragon to trigger a dispersion animation where particles emit from the dragon downward into the pool using a simple particle system with 50 spheres falling with gravity. (4) On each dispense, recalculate pH using a simplified Henderson-Hasselbalch model, validate that volume is between 1-50 mL, and update the pool liquid color by interpolating from red (pH 0) through orange, yellow, green (pH 7), to blue and purple (pH 14) using Color.lerpColors. (5) If the user overshoots past pH 7.3, allow switching to acid HCl to back-titrate. (6) Display a titration curve chart on a 2D canvas overlay plotting pH vs total volume added. (7) When pH reaches 7.0 ± 0.3, trigger a success state where the dragon plays a celebratory dispersion burst and the pool glows green. Validate all parameter inputs with clamping and display warnings for invalid ranges. The dragon should cast a colored shadow onto the pool surface matching the current reagent color. Include a reset button to restart the experiment.
